# 1 Enoch Chapter 33 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**1** And from there I went to the ends of the earth and saw there great beasts, each different from the other; and I saw birds also differing in appearance, beauty, and voice, one from the other.

**2** And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth where the heaven rests, and the portals of heaven were open.

**3** And I saw how the stars of heaven come forth, and I counted the portals out of which they proceed, and wrote down all their outlets — each individual star by itself, according to their number and their names, their courses and their positions, their times and their months — as Uriel, the holy angel who was with me, showed me.

**4** He showed me all things and wrote them down for me; he also wrote for me their names and their laws and their companies.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Ge'ez text. Chapter 33 opens the astronomical section of the second journey (chs. 33-36): the eastern star-portals. Enoch's careful record-keeping of stellar names, courses, positions, and times anticipates the full Astronomical Book (1 Enoch 72-82). Uriel resumes his role as guide. The "portals of heaven" are the openings through which the stars, sun, and moon enter and exit the sky.*
